root_cause_detail: A local ESET SSL Filter CA-issued certificate was presented to Windows SslStream; that CA is installed in Windows Root stores. Python's default OpenSSL validation rejects the intercepted chain for missing Subject Key Identifier (verify code 86). A strict certifi-backed Python context received a TWCA-issued certificate and validated successfully. No explicit environment proxy or CA override was present. This is a client/trust-path-dependent TLS interception difference, not proof of a generally invalid TPEx endpoint certificate.
smallest_safe_repair_recommendation: In a separately authorized remediation tranche, evaluate an explicit certifi-backed ssl.create_default_context passed to urllib.request.urlopen (or another supported strictly validating TLS backend) for the production acquisition client. Keep CERT_REQUIRED and hostname/SNI checking enabled, ensure certifi is a declared runtime dependency, test transport without HTTP first, and only then request fresh bounded source-acquisition authority. Do not suppress verification or change machine trust.
